title: Estimating Dynamic Causal Effects with hetiv
text: hetiv provides tools measuring identifying multi-dimensional structural shocks dynamic models using two complementary IV approaches: Heteroskedasticity-IV (Rigobon 2003, Rigobon Sack 2004, Lewis 2022, Burri Kaufmann, 2026b): exploits higher variance outcome variables policy event days relative control days identify structural shocks without requiring external instruments. Proxy-IV (Mertens Ravn 2013, Stock Watson 2018): uses external instrument (proxy) correlated shock interest uncorrelated shocks. approaches implemented local projection IV estimators following Jordà (2005), directly produce impulse response functions (IRFs) across multiple horizons. Inference based heteroskedasticity-robust standard errors default. Montiel Olea et al. (2025) show standard errors suffice local-projection impulse responses weak conditions, even though multi-step forecast errors typically serially correlated. Newey-West HAC standard errors also available via cov_type = "NW" optional robustness check. package allows multiple shocks endogenous variables. Weak-instrument HAR inference implemented via generalised minimum eigenvalue test Lewis Mertens (2025), nests classical Stock-Yogo (2005) test univariate homoskedastic case. gweakivtest() direct port Matlab files Lewis Mertens (2025) available https://karelmertens.com/research/. addition, package provides predict_shocks() predicting underlying unobserved shocks based Kalman filter, suggested Burri Kaufmann (2026a). currently work extension exploit multiple IRF horizons shock extraction. vignette demonstrates functionality using simulated four-variable VAR two structural shocks.

text: simulate data VAR(2) \(N = 4\) variables, \(E = 2\) event (policy) shocks, \(R = 4\) regular shocks, \(P = 2\) lags \(T = 500\) observations. model reads: \[y_t = \Psi \varepsilon_t + \Gamma v_t + \Phi(L) y_{t-1} + \beta X_t \ \ \text{} t\\mathcal{P}\] \[y_t =  \Gamma v_t + \Phi(L) y_{t-1} + \beta X_t \ \ \text{} t\\mathcal{C}\] \(\mathcal{P}, \mathcal{C}\) denote policy event days, respectively, \(\Psi\) impact matrix \(E\) policy event shocks \(\Gamma\) impact matrix \(R\) shocks. \(\Phi(L)\) conformable lag polynomial, \(X_t\) matrix deterministic terms. Regular shocks occur days. many regular shocks variables, covariance matrix reduced-form residuals control days full rank. policy event occurs every 10th period (approximately 10% observations). latter introduces heteroskedasticity variance-covariance matrix reduced-form residuals hetiv() exploits identify impulse response functions. Shocks drawn standard normal distribution. impact matrix lower-triangular, corresponding identifying assumption Burri Kaufmann (2026b) first shock contemporaneous effect variables, second shock contemporaneous effect first variable. Deterministic weekday patterns added variables 3 4 illustrate role controls. event indicator Ind equals 1 policy event days 0 control days. illustrate proxy-IV approach, construct noisy external instrument two event shocks adding Gaussian noise true shocks. proxy set zero control days. mirrors convention proxy-SVAR literature (Mertens Ravn, 2013; Gertler Karadi, 2015), high-frequency surprises recorded around policy announcement windows set zero otherwise. Setting proxy NA control days instead excludes days proxy-IV regressions reproduces announcement-day sample event-study literature (Nakamura Steinsson, 2018). conventions use identifying moments, first-stage reduced-form cross products involve event days ; differ sample used estimate control coefficients. use zeros default convention.
code: library(hetiv)  # Dimensions N <- 4 # variables E <- 2 # event shocks R <- 4 # regular shocks (as many as variables) P <- 2 # VAR lag order H <- 20 # IRF horizons Nevn <- 10 # Frequency of event shocks  # Impact matrix for event shocks (N x E); lower triangular for recursive ID PsiE <- matrix(0, N, E) PsiE[, 1] <- c(1.0, 0.5, 0.3, 0.2) PsiE[, 2] <- c(0.0, 1.0, -0.4, 0.3)  SigE <- 4 # event shock variance (scalar, applies to all E shocks)  # Impact matrix for regular shocks (N x R) PsiR <- matrix(0, N, R) PsiR[, 1] <- c(1.0, -0.3, 0.2, 0.1) PsiR[, 2] <- c(0.2, 1.0, -0.1, 0.4) PsiR[, 3] <- c(0.1, 0.2, 1.0, -0.2) PsiR[, 4] <- c(-0.1, 0.1, 0.3, 1.0)  # VAR coefficient matrices at lags 1 and 2 Phi <- array(0, dim = c(N, N, P)) Phi[, , 1] <- matrix(c(   0.60, 0.05, -0.04, 0.03,   0.06, 0.40, 0.05, -0.03,   -0.05, 0.04, 0.50, 0.06,   0.03, -0.03, 0.05, 0.70 ), N, N, byrow = TRUE) Phi[, , 2] <- matrix(c(   0.10, 0.03, -0.02, 0.02,   0.04, 0.10, 0.03, -0.02,   -0.03, 0.02, 0.10, 0.03,   0.02, -0.02, 0.03, 0.10 ), N, N, byrow = TRUE)  # Simulate — seed is set internally by simulatedata() Nobs <- 500 Nbin <- 100 sim <- simulatedata(   Phi = Phi, SigE = SigE, PsiE = PsiE, PsiR = PsiR,   Nobs = Nobs, Nbin = Nbin, N = N, R = R, E = E,   Nevn = Nevn, P = P, eDist = 0, seed = 42 )  # Extract simulated data and event indicator y_data <- sim$y Ind <- as.integer(sim$IndE[, 1])  # Add deterministic weekday variation into variables 3 and 4 y_data[, 3] <- y_data[, 3] + 0.5 * seq_len(Nobs) %% 5 y_data[, 4] <- y_data[, 4] + 0.3 * seq_len(Nobs) %% 5 # RNG state after simulatedata(seed = 42) is deterministic, so no extra seed needed e_proxy <- sim$eE e_proxy[, 1] <- e_proxy[, 1] + rnorm(Nobs, sd = 1) e_proxy[, 2] <- e_proxy[, 2] + rnorm(Nobs, sd = 1) e_proxy[Ind == 0, ] <- 0

code: # y: T x 1 outcome variable # Y: T x N matrix of endogenous regressors # X: T x Nx matrix of exogenous controls # Z: T x K matrix of instruments (requires K >= N)  wt <- gweakivtest(y = y, Y = Y, X = X, Z = Z)  # Inspect test statistics and critical values wt$gmin_generalized                            # generalised min-eigenvalue statistic wt$gmin_generalized_critical_value             # Lewis-Mertens sharp critical value (Stiefel) wt$gmin_generalized_critical_value_simplified  # conservative closed-form bound  # With Newey-West HAR standard errors and custom bias tolerance wt <- gweakivtest(y = y, Y = Y, X = X, Z = Z, cov_type = "NW", tau = 0.10)  # hetiv() and proxyiv() return WeakData when details = TRUE, # which contains the outcome and instrument columns needed for gweakivtest(). Note that the E endogenous variables have to be ordered first res     <- hetiv(y = y, O = O, Ind = Ind, P = 1, H = 20, E = 1, details = TRUE) weakdata <- res$WeakData  # y: outcome variable E + 1 (not used as endogenous regressor) y_w <- weakdata[, paste0("y", E + 1)] # Y: first E outcome variables (endogenous regressors) Y_w <- weakdata[, paste0("y", 1:E)] # Z: the E instruments Z_w <- weakdata[, paste0("Z", 1:E), drop = FALSE] # X: lagged ("o*"), deterministic ("x*"), and indicator ("i*") controls. # gweakivtest() adds a constant term if one is missing. ctrl <- startsWith(colnames(weakdata), "o") |   startsWith(colnames(weakdata), "x") |   startsWith(colnames(weakdata), "i") X_w <- if (any(ctrl)) weakdata[, ctrl, drop = FALSE] else matrix(numeric(0), nrow(weakdata), 0)  wt <- gweakivtest(y = y_w, Y = Y_w, X = X_w, Z = Z_w)
